clue.text: Agree to keep in touch

definitions.meaning: two accounts that match or tally are said to agree
to exchange letters with someone regularly is to stay in contact by post

explanation.surface: An invitation to stay in contact with someone, accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both matching up with something and writing letters back and forth to a friend.

clue.text: Possessive, possibly, of one item of luggage

definitions.meaning: the possessive or genitive is one example of a grammatical form a noun can take
a suitcase is a single piece of travelling baggage

explanation.surface: A grammar note musing on whether a single bag counts as possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's possessive is one inflectional category of a noun, and a suitcase is a single bag for travel.

clue.text: Bank run by cathedral?

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, used in crosswords for a cathedral

explanation.surface: A building society branch operated by a cathedral, a curious financial arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is not a building but the verb, as in banking on someone; 'by' simply puts the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to depend on them, the same trust as counting on them.

clue.text: Stogie-chewing self-seeker?…

indicators.note: chewing mangles the cigar's letters, so the word Stogie is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A selfish character chomping on a cheap cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewing' shuffles STOGIE; a stogie is a long cheap cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wholly concerned with their own interests is a self-centred person seeking advantage.

clue.text: … appoint entirely new diplomatic envoy!

indicators.note: new indicates the fifteen letters of the two words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Continuing the ellipsis: the selfish smoker should name a brand new ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges APPOINT and ENTIRELY together; the ellipsis joins this clue's surface to the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: Such an envoy is an ambassador given full powers to act on behalf of a government.

clue.text: Mace jewel placed on barrel, upturned

indicators.note: in a down clue, upturned means the whole stack is read from the bottom upwards
in a down entry, a piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone or jewel
a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: A ceremonial staff decorated with a jewel mounted on a barrel that has been tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mace' looks like the ceremonial club but is the spice; 'upturned' turns GEM over TUN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is the spice made from the lacy covering of the same seed, so the two are closely linked flavourings.

clue.text: Bend front section of Spitfire, for example

indicators.note: only the front part of the word is kept, its tail being dropped

parts.note: the Spitfire was a British Second World War fighter, an example of a military aircraft

explanation.surface: Instructions to bend the nose of a classic fighter plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spitfire is a famous British WWII fighter; take only the first half of WARPLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: To distort something out of its true shape, as heat does to timber, is to twist it.

clue.text: Get a table? That is dashed handy!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Get a table? That is dashed handy!' (10): ACCESS (get) + I.E. (that is) leaves B and L unexplained; no printed scan and no source found to supply the missing piece.
annotationWithheld.clue: Get a table? That is dashed handy!

clue.text: Sally with lovely lines

parts.note: lovely and pleasant both mean agreeable or nice
RY is short for railway, whose lines are its tracks

explanation.surface: A girl named Sally, along with some charming lines of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' is not a name but a witty remark; 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quip or jest, and a light humorous remark is a polite joke.

clue.text: Outline of hotel suite to be renovated

indicators.note: renovating rebuilds something, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A drawing of the shape of a hotel room due for a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be renovated' rearranges HOTEL SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark shape seen against a light background shows only an object's profile or outline.

clue.text: Crown came out!

indicators.note: out here means the word came is put out of order

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the crown jewels have been revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CAME; 'Crown' means the top or peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of something is its highest point, its peak or summit.

clue.text: Spreads out in the country?

parts.note: spreads looks like a verb but is the American noun for ranches, landholdings with buildings in rural areas

explanation.surface: Something unfolding across rural land.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Spreads' as a noun: a spread is a large farm or ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural homesteads with their land and buildings are farms, which Americans call spreads.

clue.text: Punctuation mark perhaps too freely scattered?

indicators.note: scattering the letters about freely signals that perhaps and too are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that a particular piece of punctuation is used far too liberally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely scattered' rearranges PERHAPS TOO; the surface nods at the much-misplaced grocer's apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: This raised comma marks possession or omitted letters in written English.

clue.text: In these court sessions, fool admits magnitude

indicators.note: admits means the first word lets the second in, enclosing it

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
magnitude and size both mean how large something is

explanation.surface: A trial where an idiot owns up to the scale of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' puts SIZE inside ASS. The assizes were periodic county courts in England and Wales, abolished in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: These were periodic sittings of judges touring the English counties to hear cases.

clue.text: A jazz-fan about to steal a tumbler

indicators.note: about means the jazz-fan's word goes round the outside of the other

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: A jazz lover poised to pinch a drinking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbler' looks like a glass but is a gymnast; 'about' wraps CAT around ROB.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is a performer of somersaults and handsprings, the same as a gymnastic circus performer.

clue.text: Succeeded with pawn and queen-sensational play!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
to hock something is to pawn it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for the Queen

explanation.surface: A chess move with pawn and queen that pays off, a thrilling game.
explanation.walkthrough: Pawn and queen suggest chess, but 'pawn' is the verb to pledge for cash; 'with' only joins pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurid melodrama or thriller is a show meant to startle its audience.

clue.text: Facial expression of one who has set cap, wantonly?

indicators.note: doing something wantonly is doing it recklessly, so the letters of set cap are thrown about

explanation.surface: Wondering what face someone pulls after setting their cap at a suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wantonly' rearranges SET CAP; to set one's cap at someone is an old idiom for trying to win them.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's look or countenance, the way their face appears, is an older sense of the word.

clue.text: Haunting memories of Ibsen's work

definitions.meaning: remembrances that trouble someone like spectres from the past
the Norwegian playwright Henrik Ibsen wrote a play of 1881 with this title

explanation.surface: Recollections that linger from a Norwegian playwright's drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectres stand for past events that keep troubling us, and the word is also the title of an Ibsen play.

clue.text: Wrong idea of motorway's fabric

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for a motorway, and the 's is read as the word is
fabric can mean the framework or structure of a building

explanation.surface: A mistaken notion about what a motorway is built of.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'motorway's' as M IS: the apostrophe s stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the wrong interpretation on something gives a mistaken understanding of it.

clue.text: Mad Hatter's warning

indicators.note: mad signals that the letters of hatter are deranged into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A caution from the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges HATTER; the surface borrows Lewis Carroll's character.
explanation.definitionFit: A menacing statement of intended harm serves as a caution to someone.

clue.text: Marat universally recognized from his bodily injury

indicators.note: from here signals that the answer is made from a reworking of the letters

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: The French revolutionary Marat, famous for the wound he suffered in his bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges MARAT plus U. Jean-Paul Marat was stabbed to death in his bath in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: A physical wound or injury to the body is the medical sense of the word.

clue.text: One may settle and try to contain the French

indicators.note: to contain means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Someone who may sort out a dispute and attempt to keep the French in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One may settle' looks like a mediator but is a person who mends; 'to contain' puts LE inside HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: One who cures soothes and calms ailments, settling a troubled body.

clue.text: Ether turns, with oxygen, to this matter

indicators.note: turns signals the letters of ether are turned about into a new order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: ether reacts with oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges ETHER, then O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This formal legal word means relating to the document or subject in hand.

clue.text: One of four running in land race, say?

definitions.text: One of four running in land race, say?

parts.words: One of four running in land race, say?
parts.note: a Landrace is a breed of pig, and a pig runs on four feet, each of which is a cooked delicacy as well

explanation.surface: A runner in a cross-country race with four entrants.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'land race' as Landrace, a breed of pig: one of its four feet is the answer. It also suggests a harness racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's foot, of which it has four, is called by this name.

clue.text: A chemist's charges

parts.note: MPS stands for Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, letters after a chemist's name

explanation.surface: The prices a pharmacist charges for things.
explanation.walkthrough: MPS, Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, is the qualification of a British chemist (pharmacist).
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical charges flowing are measured in amperes, so the units stand loosely for charges of current.

clue.text: Sara I replaced a national dress

indicators.note: replaced means one letter has taken the place of another in the name

parts.note: the letter a as written
the letter I as written

explanation.surface: Sara has swapped one outfit for a traditional costume.
explanation.walkthrough: I has replaced the final A of SARA.
explanation.definitionFit: This draped length of cloth is the traditional garment of women in India.

clue.text: Bird found in water, normally

indicators.note: found in means the letters are lying inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A seabird usually seen on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' picks the letters spanning the end of 'water' and the start of 'normally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a slender seabird with forked tail, a relative of gulls.

clue.text: Grave abuse, possible, of what is below standard

indicators.note: possible suggests one possible arrangement of the letters of grave abuse

explanation.surface: Serious mistreatment, perhaps, of something not up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges GRAVE ABUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something below the usual or mean level is inferior or not up to standard.

clue.text: Slough outbuilding

definitions.meaning: to slough is to cast off a skin, as a snake does
a small hut in the garden for tools

explanation.surface: A small hut in Slough, the Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the Berkshire town west of London but is the verb meaning to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake casts its skin, and a garden hut for tools is a simple outbuilding.

clue.text: Was this old citizen-gardener suspended?

parts.note: the Hanging Gardens were one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world, in the Mesopotamian city on the Euphrates

explanation.surface: Asking whether an elderly resident who gardens was punished by suspension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' suggests a ban but points to hanging: the Hanging Gardens were in the ancient city of Babylon, so its gardener is a citizen of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the ancient Mesopotamian capital famous for its Hanging Gardens bears this name.
